findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so code generated into projects targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework gets no attribute. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on .NET Standard 2.0 and on .NET Framework 4.0 and later. The requirement allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist. As written, 'all generated code is decorated' is not met for two of the most common library targets. The same guard appears in every template: Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver and CompositeResolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageLegacyTargetTests.GeneratedCode_IsExcludedFromCodeCoverage_OnLegacyTargets. It runs the generator with the preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK against references that contain the attribute. On head it fails: generated formatters and the resolver carry no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

findings.claim: No opt-out setting was added: the attribute is emitted unconditionally, with no GeneratorOptions/analyzer option to disable it. Ledger L7 records the answer 'Add an opt-out setting' for the codegen-templates area. That entry's question text concerns target frameworks, so the Q/A pairing looks mismatched and a human should confirm. Read as a decision, the change does not implement it.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite ledger L7 (area=codegen-templates): 'A: Add an opt-out setting'. Then check that no template emission of ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is gated by any option, and that the diff adds no option.

findings.claim: The new README text says the attribute is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. That is factually wrong: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute ships in .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+. The docs therefore justify the coverage gap with a false premise.
